- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (0.3–0.7), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and align with sentiment momentum.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for next 7 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true outcome is below 60% of 30-day forecast mean, consider sentiment-driven correction: if sentiment >0.5, reduce forecast by 1–3%; if sentiment <0.3, increase by 0.5–2% to align with market sentiment.
